notes: Recall/precision checklist for evaluating extraction quality, not an exact-match target -- a correct extraction phrases each requirement differently from source.quote below.
source.spans marks the tender.txt offsets a requirement originates from; source.quote is those spans' text, joined with ' ... ' when there is more than one span.

Exhaustive over bidder-facing, pre-award requirements in tender.txt: both text-verifiable ones (is_text_verifiable: true) and ones that describe an eligibility fact or a submission process rather than application content (is_text_verifiable: false).

No excluded_clauses list: text that is not a bidder requirement at all (SD/VOSB/VOSB clause definitions, market-research and brand-name-justification narrative, evaluation-factor boilerplate) is simply absent here.
single_best_price_quote is is_mandatory: false because the solicitation uses "requested", not "must", for this item.

is_text_verifiable is true only when the tender itself instructs the bidder to write/represent something specific in their submission (a checkbox, a required statement, a document to attach). sam_registration_required, sdvosb_certification_required, and los_requirements_met are false: the tender states plain eligibility/performance facts (SAM registration, VIP/VetCert listing, actually meeting the LOS subcontracting limits) with no instruction to represent them in the quote text -- unlike los_compliance_assertion (explicit instruction to assert compliance in the email) or far_52_212_3_reps_and_certs (an explicit required document).

los_requirements_met and los_compliance_assertion are two separate topics from one tender sentence pair: the first ('Offeror must meet LOS requirements') is a substantive fact application text cannot verify; the second ('Compliance... must be asserted... in the email') is a checkable procedural instruction -- whether the email contains such an assertion at all.

eft_indicator_if_applicable and quote_signed_and_dated were added after auditing a real run's unexplained predicted requirements against tender.txt directly -- both are genuine bidder-facing content the earlier 14-topic list missed. Most of the other unexplained predictions from that audit are either SD/VOSB or LOS clause-definition/evaluation-factor boilerplate (correctly out of scope, matching the exclusion rule above) or restatements of an existing topic anchored elsewhere in tender.txt (a genuine dedup/matching miss, not a fixture gap) -- notably the '(c) Period for acceptance of Quotes' clause, which is marked 'N/A (Not Applicable)' for this solicitation right after its boilerplate text, so it is correctly out of scope too.
tender.txt was extracted from the source .docx with python-docx; non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) were normalized to regular spaces so citation offsets line up with plain-text extraction.

quote_content_minimum_elements was split into 7 topics (solicitation_number_stated, time_specified_for_receipt_stated, quoter_contact_info_stated, technical_description_stated, warranty_terms_stated, price_and_discount_terms_stated, remit_to_address_stated): each item has independent pass/fail meaning (a quote could state the solicitation number but omit the technical description), unlike a single indivisible form.
